name: Multiple Linear Regression
formula: drugs ~ o + c + e + a + n
description: Linear regression of illegal drug use on Big Five personality scores. Family: gaussian.

name: Regression Splines — Explicit Intercept
description: Spline basis regression of bloom day-of-year on year, with explicit intercept term in the basis expansion. Family: gaussian.

name: Regression Splines — Absorbed Intercept
description: Spline basis regression of bloom day-of-year on year, with model intercept absorbed (not explicit in the basis). Family: gaussian.

name: Hierarchical Linear Regression — Pig Growth
description: Mixed-effects model of pig weight over time with random slope and intercept per pig. Family: gaussian.

name: Hierarchical Linear Regression — Sleep Deprivation
description: Mixed-effects model of reaction time on days of sleep deprivation with random slope and intercept per subject. Family: gaussian.

name: Radon — Complete Pooling
description: Complete pooling model: single intercept per floor type, ignoring county structure. Family: gaussian.

name: Radon — No Pooling
description: No-pooling model: separate intercept for each county-floor combination. Family: gaussian.

name: Radon — Partial Pooling (Intercept Only)
description: Partial pooling with random county intercepts, no floor predictor. Family: gaussian.

name: Radon — Partial Pooling with Floor
description: Partial pooling with floor as fixed effect and random county intercepts. Family: gaussian.

name: Radon — Varying Slopes
description: Partial pooling with random slope and intercept for floor by county. Family: gaussian.

name: Radon — County-Level Uranium Predictor
description: Partial pooling with floor and county-level uranium predictor (log_u). Family: gaussian.

name: Strack RRR — Simple Random Effects
description: Simple model with condition as fixed effect and random participant intercepts. Family: gaussian.

name: Strack RRR — Full Crossed Random Effects
description: Full model with condition, age, gender, random participant intercepts, and crossed random effects for study and stimulus. Family: gaussian.

name: Shooter Task — Rate (No Target Effect)
description: Reaction rate modeled by race × object interaction with crossed random effects per subject, without target random effects. Family: gaussian.

name: Shooter Task — Rate (With Target Effect)
formula: rate ~ S(race) * S(object) + (S(race) * S(object) | subject) + (S(object) | target)
description: Reaction rate modeled by race × object interaction with crossed random effects for both subject and target. Family: gaussian.

name: Shooter Task — Binary Shoot Decision
description: Binary shoot/don't-shoot decision modeled by race × object interaction with crossed random effects for subject and target. Family: bernoulli.

name: Fixed/Random Effects — Naive Model
description: Naive logistic regression ignoring group structure entirely. Family: bernoulli.

name: Fixed/Random Effects — Fixed Effects Model
description: Fixed effects logistic regression with a dummy indicator per group. Family: bernoulli.

name: Fixed/Random Effects — Random Effects Model
description: Multilevel logistic regression with random group intercepts. Family: bernoulli.

name: Fixed/Random Effects — Mundlak Machine
description: Mundlak machine: random intercepts plus group-mean of x to separate within/between effects. Family: bernoulli.

name: Robust Regression — Gaussian Family
description: Standard linear regression on data with outliers; used as baseline. Family: gaussian.

name: Robust Regression — Student's t Family
description: Robust linear regression using Student's t family, which down-weights outliers. Family: t.

name: Predict New Groups
description: Mixed-effects model predicting FVC with random slopes per patient; demonstrates out-of-sample prediction for new groups. Family: gaussian.

name: Polynomial Regression — Falling Ball (Explicit)
description: Polynomial regression using inline transformation `I(t**2)` to recover gravitational constant from falling ball data. Family: gaussian.

name: Polynomial Regression — Falling Ball (Curly-Brace Syntax)
description: Same as :poly_falling_explicit but using Bambi's alternative curly-brace inline transformation syntax. Family: gaussian.

name: Polynomial Regression — Falling Ball (Pre-Computed Column)
description: Polynomial regression using a pre-computed `tsquared` column rather than inline transformation. Family: gaussian.

name: Polynomial Regression — Projectile (Power Basis)
description: Explicit quadratic polynomial regression on projectile data with both linear and quadratic terms. Family: gaussian.

name: Polynomial Regression — Projectile (poly() Syntax)
description: Quadratic polynomial regression using Bambi's `poly()` function with raw (non-orthogonal) polynomials. Family: gaussian.

name: Polynomial Regression — Multi-Planet
description: Planet-specific quadratic coefficient interacted with `Planet` to recover different gravitational constants per planet. Family: gaussian.

name: Logistic Regression — Vote Intention
description: Logistic regression of Clinton vote on party ID and party-age interaction. Family: bernoulli.

name: Model Comparison — Linear
description: Linear logistic regression of income on sex, race, age, and weekly hours worked. Family: bernoulli.

name: Model Comparison — Quadratic
formula: income['>50K'] ~ sex + race + scale(age) + I(scale(age)**2) + scale(hs_week) + I(scale(hs_week)**2)
description: Quadratic logistic regression adding squared age and hours terms. Family: bernoulli.

name: Model Comparison — Cubic
formula: income['>50K'] ~ sex + race + scale(age) + I(scale(age)**2) + I(scale(age)**3) + scale(hs_week) + I(scale(hs_week)**2) + I(scale(hs_week)**3)
description: Cubic logistic regression adding cubic age and hours terms. Family: bernoulli.

name: Hierarchical Binomial — No Pooling
description: Non-hierarchical binomial model: separate intercept per player. Family: binomial.

name: Hierarchical Binomial — Partial Pooling
description: Hierarchical binomial model with random player intercepts. Family: binomial.

name: Alternative Links — Logit
description: Binomial regression with logit link (default). Family: binomial, link="logit".

name: Alternative Links — Probit
description: Binomial regression with probit link. Family: binomial, link="probit".

name: Alternative Links — Complementary Log-Log
description: Binomial regression with complementary log-log link. Family: binomial, link="cloglog".

name: Wald Regression — Insurance Claims (Wald Family)
description: Wald (inverse Gaussian) regression of claim costs on age category (as categorical), gender and area. Family: wald, link="log".

name: Gamma Regression — Insurance Claims (Gamma Family)
description: Gamma regression of claim costs on age category (numeric), gender and area. Family: gamma, link="log".

name: Negative Binomial — Main Effects
description: Negative binomial regression of student absences on program type and math score. Family: negativebinomial.

name: Negative Binomial — Interaction
description: Negative binomial regression adding program-by-math interaction term. Family: negativebinomial.

name: Count Regression with Offset — Poisson
description: Poisson regression of roach counts with log-exposure offset. Family: poisson.

name: Count Regression with Offset — Negative Binomial
description: Negative binomial regression of roach counts with log-exposure offset; accounts for overdispersion relative to Poisson. Family: negativebinomial.

name: Beta Regression — Intercept Only (Probabilities)
description: Intercept-only beta regression on synthetic probability data. Family: beta.

name: Beta Regression — Coin Dirt
description: Beta regression of probability on coin dirt differential. Family: beta.

name: Beta Regression — Batting Average Intercept Only
description: Intercept-only beta regression on baseball batting averages. Family: beta.

name: Beta Regression — Batting Average with Shift Predictor
description: Beta regression of batting average on prior-year batting average. Family: beta.

name: Categorical Regression — Toy Dataset
description: Categorical regression on three Gaussian classes. Family: categorical.

name: Categorical Regression — Iris Species
description: Categorical regression predicting iris species from morphological measurements. Family: categorical.

name: Categorical Regression — Alligator Food Choice
description: Categorical regression of alligator food choice on body length and sex. Family: categorical.

name: Circular Regression — Von Mises Family
description: Circular regression of periwinkle direction on distance using von Mises distribution. Family: vonmises.

name: Circular Regression — Gaussian Comparison
description: Gaussian regression of circular direction data; used as a misspecified comparison model against the von Mises. Family: gaussian.

name: Quantile Regression — p10 (Asymmetric Laplace)
description: Spline regression targeting the 10th percentile of BMI. Family: asymmetriclaplace, kappa=0.1.

name: Quantile Regression — p50 (Asymmetric Laplace)
description: Spline regression targeting the 50th percentile (median) of BMI. Family: asymmetriclaplace, kappa=0.5.

name: Quantile Regression — p90 (Asymmetric Laplace)
description: Spline regression targeting the 90th percentile of BMI. Family: asymmetriclaplace, kappa=0.9.

name: Quantile Regression — Gaussian Comparison
description: Spline regression using Gaussian family; used as comparison model to quantile approach. Family: gaussian.

name: MrP — Multilevel Regression and Post-Stratification
description: Multilevel binomial regression with crossed random effects for state, ethnicity, education and interactions; used for post-stratification. Family: binomial.

name: Zero Inflated Poisson — Mu Component
description: ZIP mu component: models the expected count given non-zero. Family: zero_inflated_poisson.

name: Zero Inflated Poisson — Psi Component
description: ZIP psi component: models the probability of excess zeros. Family: zero_inflated_poisson.

name: Hurdle Poisson — Mu Component
description: Hurdle Poisson mu component: models the expected count given positive. Family: hurdle_poisson.

name: Hurdle Poisson — Psi Component
description: Hurdle Poisson psi component: models the probability of a non-zero outcome. Family: hurdle_poisson.

name: Ordinal Regression — Trolley Intercept Only
description: Cumulative ordinal model with only threshold parameters, no predictors. Family: cumulative.

name: Ordinal Regression — Trolley Action/Intention/Contact
formula: response ~ 0 + action + intention + contact + action:intention + contact:intention
description: Cumulative ordinal model with action, intention, contact and their interactions. Family: cumulative.

name: Ordinal Regression — HR Years at Company
description: Sequential ratio (sratio) ordinal model predicting years at company from total working years. Family: sratio.

name: Distributional Models — Constant Alpha
description: Gamma regression with a single (constant) shape parameter alpha. Family: gamma.

name: Distributional Models — Varying Alpha
description: Distributional gamma regression: compound formula models both mu and alpha as functions of x. Family: gamma.

name: Distributional Models — Bikes Spline
formula: count ~ 0 + bs(hour, 8, intercept=True)  +  alpha ~ 0 + bs(hour, 8, intercept=True)
description: Distributional gamma regression on hourly bike count data; both mu and alpha modeled with spline basis functions. Family: gamma.

name: HSGP 1D — Basic
description: Hilbert-space Gaussian process approximation on 1D synthetic data. Family: gaussian.

name: HSGP 1D — Centered Parameterization
description: HSGP with centered parameterization on 1D synthetic data. Family: gaussian.

name: HSGP 1D — By Group (Shared Covariance)
description: HSGP on GAM data with group-specific processes sharing covariance parameters. Family: gaussian.

name: HSGP 1D — By Group (No Shared Covariance)
formula: y ~ 0 + hsgp(x2, by=fac, m=12, c=1.5, share_cov=False)
description: HSGP on GAM data with group-specific processes and independent covariance parameters. Family: gaussian.

name: HSGP 2D — Isotropic
description: Isotropic 2D Hilbert-space Gaussian process on synthetic data. Family: gaussian.

name: HSGP 2D — By Group (Shared Covariance)
formula: outcome ~ 0 + hsgp(x, y, by=group, c=1.5, m=10)
description: 2D HSGP with group-specific processes sharing covariance parameters. Family: gaussian.

name: HSGP 2D — By Group (No Shared Covariance)
formula: outcome ~ 0 + hsgp(x, y, by=group, c=1.5, m=10, share_cov=False)
description: 2D HSGP with group-specific processes and independent covariance parameters. Family: gaussian.

name: HSGP 2D — Anisotropic
formula: outcome ~ 0 + hsgp(x, y, c=1.5, m=10, iso=False)
description: Anisotropic 2D HSGP allowing different length scales per dimension. Family: gaussian.

name: HSGP 2D — Spatial Poisson Count Data
formula: Count ~ 0 + Year + X1:Year + (1|Site) + hsgp(Lon, Lat, by=Year, m=5, c=1.5)
description: Poisson regression combining fixed effects, random site intercepts, and a 2D spatial HSGP term varying by year. Family: poisson.

name: Survival Model — Intercept Only
description: Exponential survival model with only an intercept (constant hazard). Family: exponential, link="log".

name: Survival Model — Color Effect
description: Exponential survival model with cat color as a predictor. Family: exponential, link="log".

name: Discrete Time Survival — Simulated Data
description: Bernoulli survival model with complementary log-log link on synthetic discrete-time data. Family: bernoulli, link="cloglog".

name: Discrete Time Survival — Binomial Child Mortality
formula: p(events, at_risk) ~ sex + socBranch + period + scale(birth_decade)
description: Binomial discrete-time survival model on Swedish child mortality data. Family: binomial, link="cloglog".

name: Discrete Time Survival — Spline Baseline Hazard
formula: p(events, at_risk) ~ sex + socBranch + bs(period, df=4) + scale(birth_decade)
description: Binomial discrete-time survival with spline baseline hazard. Family: binomial, link="cloglog".

name: Discrete Time Survival — Poisson Alternative
formula: events ~ sex + socBranch + period + scale(birth_decade) + offset(log(at_risk))
description: Poisson formulation of discrete-time survival with log-offset for person-time. Family: poisson.

name: Continuous Time Survival — Weibull
description: Weibull survival model on synthetic data with treatment and age effects. Family: weibull.

name: Continuous Time Survival — Retention Fixed Effects
formula: censored(month, censoring) ~ C(gender) + C(level) + C(field) + sentiment + intention
description: Weibull survival model of employee tenure with fixed effects only. Family: weibull.

name: Continuous Time Survival — Retention Random Effects
formula: censored(month, censoring) ~ C(gender) + C(level) + sentiment + intention + (1|field)
description: Weibull survival model of employee tenure with random intercepts for field. Family: weibull.

name: Orthogonal Polynomial — Explicit Quadratic
description: Explicit (raw) quadratic polynomial on projectile data. Family: gaussian.

name: Orthogonal Polynomial — poly() Degree 2
description: Orthogonal polynomial degree 2 on projectile data. Family: gaussian.

name: Orthogonal Polynomial — MPG Linear
description: Linear regression of fuel efficiency on horsepower; baseline model. Family: gaussian.

name: Orthogonal Polynomial — MPG Quadratic
description: Orthogonal polynomial degree 2 regression of mpg on horsepower. Family: gaussian.

name: Orthogonal Polynomial — MPG Degree Comparison
description: Orthogonal polynomial regression template for degree ∈ 1:9; used for model comparison. Family: gaussian.

name: Plot Predictions — Linear Regression (mtcars)
description: Linear regression of fuel efficiency on horsepower, weight, cylinders and gear. Family: gaussian.

name: Plot Predictions — Negative Binomial (Student Absences)
description: Negative binomial regression of student absences; dataset requires Stata loading (see :negative_binomial). Placeholder DataFrame() used here. Family: negativebinomial.

name: Plot Predictions — Logistic Regression (Movies)
description: Logistic regression of "certified fresh" rating on film length and genre style. Family: bernoulli.

name: Plot Predictions — Distributional Gamma
description: Distributional gamma regression on synthetic data; same model as :distributional_var_alpha. Family: gamma.

name: Plot Comparisons — ZIP Fish Count
description: Zero-inflated Poisson model of fish catch count. Family: zero_inflated_poisson.

name: Plot Comparisons — Logistic Titanic Survival
description: Logistic regression of Titanic survival on passenger class, sex and age with interactions. Family: bernoulli.

name: Plot Slopes — Main Effects
description: Logistic regression of well-switching on distance, arsenic level and education. Family: bernoulli.

name: Plot Slopes — With Interactions
formula: switch ~ dist100 + arsenic + educ4 + dist100:educ4 + arsenic:educ4
description: Logistic regression adding education interaction terms with distance and arsenic. Family: bernoulli.

name: Using Other Samplers — JAX-Based Samplers
description: Linear regression on synthetic data; demonstrates blackjax, numpyro and nutpie backends. Family: gaussian.

name: Custom Families — Standard Binomial GLMM
description: Standard binomial GLMM for contagious bovine pleuropneumonia incidence across 4 periods.

name: Custom Families — Beta-Binomial GLMM
description: Custom `beta_binomial2` family; `vint` passes integer auxiliary data (herd size) to the custom family. Accounts for extra-binomial overdispersion.

name: Distributional Regression — Location-Scale Normal
description: Distributional model for both mean and log(sigma) as functions of group; demonstrates that the two groups differ in both location and scale.

name: Distributional Regression — Negative Binomial Counts
description: Negative binomial model for fishing trip catch counts; no zero-inflation component.

name: Distributional Regression — Zero-Inflated Poisson
formula: bf(count ~ persons + child + camper, zi ~ child)
description: Zero-inflated Poisson; `zi` sub-model predicts structural-zero probability from `child`.

name: Distributional Regression — Smooth GAM
description: Both mean and log(sigma) modeled as smooth splines; shared random group effects.

name: Handle Missing Values — Multiple Imputation
description: Fit to multiply-imputed datasets via `brm_multiple`; standard regression template on complete cases from each imputed dataset.

name: Handle Missing Values — Joint Imputation Model
formula: bf(bmi | mi() ~ age * mi(chl)) + bf(chl | mi() ~ age) + set_rescor(FALSE)
description: Joint model: simultaneously imputes `chl` while modelling `bmi`; `mi()` marks imputed variables; `set_rescor(FALSE)` removes residual correlations between equations.

name: Handle Missing Values — Measurement Error Variant
formula: bf(bmi | mi() ~ age * mi(chl)) + bf(chl | mi(se = se_chl) ~ age) + set_rescor(FALSE)
description: Variant: `chl` measured with known standard error `se_chl`; propagates measurement uncertainty into the joint imputation model.

name: Monotonic Effects — Main Effect
description: Monotonic main effect of ordered income; `mo()` constrains the response to be monotonically increasing or decreasing across ordered categories.

name: Monotonic Effects — Numeric Comparison
description: Comparison: standard numeric predictor, ignoring the ordinal structure of income.

name: Monotonic Effects — Nominal Factor Comparison
description: Comparison: unordered factor coding, ignores both ordinal structure and monotonicity.

name: Monotonic Effects — Interaction with Age
description: Interaction of monotonic income effect with age group.

name: Monotonic Effects — City-Level Random Slopes
description: Adds city-level random slopes for the monotonic income effect.

name: Multivariate Models — Compact mvbind Syntax
description: Compact syntax: one formula for both responses; correlated random effects via shared labels `p` and `q`; `set_rescor(TRUE)` adds residual correlations.

name: Multivariate Models — Explicit Separate Formulas
formula: bf(tarsus ~ sex + hatchdate + (1|p|fosternest) + (1|q|dam)) + bf(back ~ sex + hatchdate + (1|p|fosternest) + (1|q|dam)) + set_rescor(TRUE)
description: Equivalent explicit syntax with separate `bf()` per response; same model as `:btdata_compact` but with individually specified sub-formulas.

name: Multivariate Models — Skew-Normal with Splines
formula: bf(tarsus ~ sex + s(hatchdate, k=5) + (1|p|fosternest) + (1|q|dam), family = skew_normal()) + bf(back ~ sex + s(hatchdate, k=5) + (1|p|fosternest) + (1|q|dam)) + set_rescor(TRUE)
description: Extended model: skew-normal family for `tarsus`, smooth spline for `hatchdate` in both sub-models.

name: Nonlinear Models — Exponential Decay
formula: bf(y ~ b1 * exp(b2 * x), b1 + b2 ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: Nonlinear exponential model; `nl=TRUE` enables custom nonlinear predictors; `b1 + b2 ~ 1` declares both as intercept-only submodels.

name: Nonlinear Models — Linear Comparison
description: Standard linear model on the same exponential-decay data; baseline comparison.

name: Nonlinear Models — Weibull Loss Development
formula: bf(cum ~ ult * (1 - exp(-(dev/theta)^omega)), ult ~ 1 + (1|AY), omega ~ 1, theta ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: Nonlinear Weibull loss development curve; `ult` (ultimate loss) varies by accident year; `omega` = shape, `theta` = scale.

name: Phylogenetic Models — Simple Random Effect
description: Phylogenetic random effect only; `A` is the phylogenetic covariance matrix.

name: Phylogenetic Models — Additional Residual Effect
description: Adds a species-level residual random effect on top of the phylogenetic effect; `(1|phylo)` captures species-specific deviations not explained by phylogeny.

name: Phylogenetic Models — Repeated Observations
description: Phylogenetic effect plus within-species random effect for 5 repeated observations per species.

name: Phylogenetic Models — Meta-Analysis
description: Meta-analytic model; known SE derived from `N`; `se()` passes known measurement error; random study intercept captures between-species heterogeneity.

name: Phylogenetic Models — Poisson Family
description: Poisson GLMM with phylogenetic random effect; models count phenotype data.

name: Globe Tossing
description: Binomial likelihood for estimating p(water) from a globe-tossing experiment. `family = binomial(link = "identity")`; `0 + Intercept` fixes the link to identity, estimating `p` directly.

name: Heights and Weights — Intercept Only
description: Intercept-only Gaussian regression on adult heights (age >= 18, n=352). Used as a prior predictive / baseline model.

name: Heights and Weights — Linear Regression
description: Simple linear regression of height on mean-centered weight in adults (age >= 18). `weight_c = weight - mean(weight)`.

name: Heights and Weights — Quadratic Polynomial
description: Quadratic polynomial regression of height on standardized weight using the full dataset (all ages). `weight_s` = standardized weight, `weight_s2 = weight_s^2`.

name: Heights and Weights — Cubic Polynomial
description: Cubic polynomial regression of height on standardized weight using the full dataset (all ages). `weight_s3 = weight_s^3`.

name: Heights and Weights — Nonlinear Exponential Growth
formula: bf(height ~ a + exp(lb) * weight_c, a ~ 1, lb ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: Nonlinear exponential growth model for height on mean-centered weight in adults (age >= 18). `weight_c = weight - mean(weight)`.

name: Heights and Weights — Nonlinear Volume Model
description: Lognormal nonlinear model treating body weight as a scaled cylinder. `w` = weight, `h` = height. Models body weight as a scaled cylinder volume.

name: Cherry Blossoms — B-Spline Regression
description: `B` is a B-spline basis matrix (each column is a basis function); constructed via `bs(year, knots=iknots)` in R with ~17 basis columns.

name: Waffle Divorce — Age Predicts Divorce
description: Simple regression of standardized divorce rate on standardized median age at marriage. `D` = standardized Divorce, `A` = standardized MedianAgeMarriage.

name: Waffle Divorce — Marriage Rate Predicts Divorce
description: Simple regression of standardized divorce rate on standardized marriage rate. `D` = standardized Divorce, `M` = standardized Marriage.

name: Waffle Divorce — Multiple Regression (M's effect vanishes)
description: Multiple regression; M's effect vanishes after conditioning on A, revealing a spurious association between marriage rate and divorce.

name: Waffle Divorce — Mediator Regression (A predicts M)
description: Mediator regression: age at marriage predicts marriage rate. Part of the causal model where A -> M -> D and A -> D.

name: Waffle Divorce — Multivariate Simultaneous Causal Model
formula: bf(D ~ 1 + M + A) + bf(M ~ 1 + A) + set_rescor(FALSE)
description: Multivariate brms model; simultaneous causal model for D and M with residual correlation disabled via `set_rescor(FALSE)`.

name: Waffle Divorce — Measurement Error Model
description: Measurement error model from Ch 15; `D_sd` is the known standard error of the divorce estimate (approximated as 0.1 * |D| + 0.01). `D_obs` is the noisy observation.

name: Milk Energy — Neocortex Predictor
description: Positive association between neocortex percentage and kcal per gram before controlling for body mass. Uses complete cases (n=12) with non-missing neocortex.perc.

name: Milk Energy — Log Body Mass Predictor
description: Negative association; larger species produce less calorie-dense milk. Uses complete cases (n=12) with non-missing neocortex.perc.

name: Milk Energy — Neocortex and Mass (Masked Association)
description: Both effects revealed simultaneously — the masked association. Uses complete cases (n=12) with non-missing neocortex.perc.

name: Milk Energy — Clade Index Model
description: Clade index model with one intercept per primate clade, no overall intercept. Uses complete cases (n=12) with non-missing neocortex.perc.

name: Milk Energy — Joint Missing-Data Model
formula: bf(k ~ 1 + mi(b) + m) + bf(b | mi() ~ 1) + set_rescor(FALSE)
description: Joint missing-data model from Ch 15; `b` = neocortex.perc with missing values treated as partially observed. Uses the full dataset (all 29 species, including those with missing neocortex data).

name: Plant Growth — Baseline (No Treatment Effect)
description: Baseline model with no treatment effect. Growth proportional to initial height.

name: Plant Growth — Post-Treatment Bias
formula: bf(h1 ~ h0 * (a + t * treatment + f * fungus), a + t + f ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: Post-treatment bias: treatment effect absorbed by conditioning on fungus (a mediator). Including fungus blocks the path from treatment to h1.

name: Plant Growth — Causal Model (Excluding Mediator)
formula: bf(h1 ~ h0 * (a + t * treatment), a + t ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: Causal model: treatment effect recovered by excluding fungus (the mediator). This gives an unbiased estimate of the total effect of treatment on growth.

name: Happiness — Collider Bias (Spurious Age Effect)
description: `mid` = marriage as index; conditioning on marriage (a collider) induces a spurious negative association between age and happiness.

name: Happiness — Causal Model (No Age Effect)
description: No conditioning on marriage; age has no direct effect on happiness in this causal model.

name: Terrain Ruggedness — Pooled Model
description: Pooled model ignoring continent. `log_gdp_std` = log GDP standardized to mean, `rugged_std_c` = ruggedness standardized and centered.

name: Terrain Ruggedness — Continent Intercepts
description: Continent intercepts via index `cid`; same ruggedness slope for Africa and Other. `cid` = "Africa" or "Other".

name: Terrain Ruggedness — Nonlinear Continent Slopes
formula: bf(log_gdp_std ~ 0 + a + b * rugged_std_c, a ~ 0 + cid, b ~ 0 + cid, nl = TRUE)
description: Continent-specific intercepts AND slopes; ruggedness hurts GDP outside Africa but helps within Africa.

name: Tulips — Additive Water and Shade Effects
description: Additive model; `water_cent` and `shade_cent` are mean-centered. No interaction term.

name: Tulips — Water × Shade Interaction
description: Interaction model: the effect of water on blooms depends on shade level.

name: Distributional Model — Heteroscedastic Gaussian
description: Distributional model: both mean and log(`sigma`) have their own sub-models. `sigma` grows with `x`, producing heteroscedastic residuals.

name: Chimpanzees — Intercept Only
description: Intercept-only binomial; baseline probability of pulling left across all actors and treatments.

name: Chimpanzees — Actor-Indexed Intercepts and Treatment Effects
formula: bf(pulled_left | trials(1) ~ a + b, a ~ 0 + actor, b ~ 0 + treatment, nl = TRUE)
description: Actor-indexed intercepts plus treatment effects; no pooling across actors.

name: Chimpanzees — Multilevel Partial Pooling
formula: bf(pulled_left | trials(1) ~ a + b, a ~ 1 + (1 | actor) + (1 | block), b ~ 0 + treatment, nl = TRUE)
description: Multilevel model with partial pooling across actors and blocks. Adaptive regularization via hierarchical priors on actor and block intercepts.

name: Chimpanzees — Varying Slopes by Treatment
formula: pulled_left | trials(1) ~ 0 + treatment + (0 + treatment | actor) + (0 + treatment | block)
description: Varying slopes; each actor and block has its own treatment-effect vector.

name: UC Berkeley Admissions — Gender Gap
description: `gid` = gender index; apparent gender gap in admission rates before conditioning on department.

name: UC Berkeley Admissions — Gender + Department
formula: bf(admit | trials(applications) ~ a + d, a ~ 0 + gid, d ~ 0 + dept, nl = TRUE)
description: Gender and department effects; gender gap disappears after conditioning on department (Simpson's paradox).

name: UC Berkeley Admissions — Beta-Binomial
description: Custom beta-binomial family from Ch 12; `vint` passes integer auxiliary data (applications count).

name: Kline Island — Intercept-Only Poisson
description: Intercept-only Poisson (log link); baseline tool count model.

name: Kline Island — Contact-Indexed Intercepts and Log-Population Slopes
formula: bf(total_tools ~ a + b * log_pop_std, a + b ~ 0 + cid, nl = TRUE)
description: Contact-index intercepts and slopes on log-population. `cid` = contact level (high/low).

name: Kline Island — Scientific Power-Law Model
formula: bf(total_tools ~ exp(a) * population^b / g, a + b ~ 0 + cid, g ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: Scientific power-law model with identity link; `a`, `b` vary by contact level `cid`.

name: Kline Island — Gaussian Process over Geography
formula: bf(total_tools ~ exp(a) * population^b / g, a ~ 1 + gp(lat_adj, lon2_adj, scale=FALSE), b + g ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: Power-law model where `a` has a Gaussian process prior over geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude). Requires Kline2 dataset.

name: Trolley — Intercept Only (6 Thresholds)
description: Intercept-only cumulative ordinal model; 6 thresholds estimated for the 7-point response scale.

name: Trolley — Action, Contact, and Intention Effects
formula: response ~ 1 + action + contact + intention + intention:action + intention:contact
description: Action, contact, and intention effects (with interactions) on moral acceptability ratings.

name: Trolley — Monotonic Education Effect
description: Monotonic effect of ordered education; `edu_new` = integer-coded `edu` (1–8). `mo()` constrains the effect to be monotonically increasing.

name: Reed Frogs — No-Pooling Model
description: No-pooling model; one parameter per tank. Each tank gets its own intercept with no sharing of information.

name: Reed Frogs — Partial Pooling via Multilevel Model
description: Partial pooling; adaptive regularization via multilevel model. Tank-level intercepts share a common hyperprior.

name: Café Visit Times — Varying Slopes
description: Varying intercepts AND slopes; café-level covariance between them. The afternoon effect on wait time differs across cafés.

name: Primates — OLS Without Phylogeny
description: Brain size ~ body mass + group size; phylogeny ignored. All variables log-standardized.

name: Primates — Phylogenetic Regression
description: Same as OLS model plus phylogenetic correlation matrix `R` passed via `data2`. `R` is built from a phylogenetic tree, e.g. via `ape::vcv.phylo()`.

name: Moralizing Gods — Missing-Data Handling
description: Do moralizing gods predict / follow the emergence of writing? Rows with missing `moralizing_gods` or `writing` are dropped.

name: Panda Nuts — Nonlinear Learning-Curve Model
formula: bf(n_panda ~ seconds * phi * (1 - exp(-k * age_s))^theta, phi + k + theta ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: `poisson(link = identity)`; `n_panda = success`; `phi` = asymptotic rate, `k` = growth rate, `theta` = shape; `age_s` = standardized age.

name: Lynx and Hare — AR(1) Autoregressive Model
description: AR(1) autoregressive model for hare population using the full dataset (missings present in lag variables).

name: Lynx and Hare — Lag-1 Regression
description: Equivalent lag-1 regression; `Hare_1` = lag of `Hare`. Uses dropmissing dataset (d2, n=20).

name: Lynx and Hare — Missing-Data Model for Lagged Hare
description: Treating lagged `Hare` as partially observed/missing. Uses the full dataset with first-row `Hare_1` as missing.

name: Lynx and Hare — Bivariate VAR(1)
formula: bf(Hare ~ 0 + Intercept + Hare_1 + Lynx_1) + bf(Lynx ~ 0 + Intercept + Lynx_1 + Hare_1) + set_rescor(FALSE)
description: Bivariate VAR(1); lognormal family. `Lynx` feeds back on `Hare`. Uses dropmissing dataset (d2, n=20).

name: Blue Tit Morphology — Intercept Only
description: Intercept-only multivariate model; establishes baseline residual correlation between tarsus length and back coloration.

name: Blue Tit Morphology — Full Model
formula: mvbind(tarsus, back) ~ sex + hatchdate + (1 | p | fosternest) + (1 | q | dam)
description: Full model; `p`/`q` labels allow correlated random effects across responses. Sex and hatch date as fixed effects; foster nest and dam as random effects.

name: Blue Tit Morphology — Sex × Hatchdate Interaction
formula: mvbind(tarsus, back) ~ sex * hatchdate + (1 | p | fosternest) + (1 | q | dam)
description: Adds `sex` × `hatchdate` interaction to the full model.

name: Coin-Flip — Bernoulli Intercept
description: Intercept-only Bernoulli model; identity link estimates `p` directly from 50 trials with 15 successes.

name: Coin-Flip — Two-Mint Separate Intercepts
description: Separate Bernoulli intercept per mint; no intercept centering. Mint 1: 6/8 heads, mint 2: 2/7.

name: Hierarchical Bernoulli — Therapeutic Touch
description: Hierarchical Bernoulli model with partial pooling across 28 healers; logit link.

name: Hierarchical Binomial — MLB Batting Average
description: Hierarchical binomial model; players nested within positions; estimates batting average with partial pooling.

name: Binomial Recall — Separate Probability per Condition
description: Separate binomial recall probability per condition; no intercept centering. Six conditions with distinct true probabilities.

name: Binomial Recall — Pooled Single Intercept
description: Pooled single intercept model for memory recall; baseline / comparison model ignoring condition differences.

name: Two-Group IQ — Single-Group Baseline
description: Single-group Gaussian model on IQ scores; prior-predictive / baseline before conditioning on group.

name: Two-Group IQ — Heteroscedastic Groups
description: Two groups with group-specific mean AND sigma; student-t family for robustness against outliers.

name: Calcium RCT — Separate Group Means
description: Separate group means for calcium vs. placebo; Gaussian (or student-t for robustness). Outcome is blood-pressure decrease in mm Hg.

name: Simple Linear Regression — Height Predicts Weight
description: Simple linear regression with z-standardized predictors; student-t family for robustness. Uses n=300 adults.

name: Hierarchical Linear Regression — Varying Intercepts and Slopes
description: Hierarchical model with varying intercepts and slopes per subject; `||` = uncorrelated random effects; z-standardized predictors.

name: Income by Family Size — Measurement-Error Model
formula: median_income_z | se(se_z, sigma = TRUE) ~ 1 + family_size_z + I(family_size_z^2) + (1 + family_size_z + I(family_size_z^2) || State)
description: Measurement-error model via `| se()`; quadratic trend in family size; state-level random slopes. Accounts for known standard error in the outcome.

name: Guber 1999 — Base Multiple Regression
description: Multiple regression of SAT score on spending and percent taking SAT; percent taking is a suppressor variable.

name: Guber 1999 — Complement Proportion Predictor
description: Adds complementary proportion (prop_not_take_z = 1 - prcnt_take); explicit centering via `0 + Intercept`.

name: Guber 1999 — Interaction Term
description: Adds interaction_z = spend_z * prcnt_take_z (standardized product); student-t for robustness.

name: Fruitfly — Hierarchical One-Way ANOVA
description: ANOVA as hierarchical model; partial pooling across companion types for longevity.

name: Fruitfly — Pooled Baseline
description: Pooled / no-group baseline model for longevity; comparison model with no companion-type structure.

name: Fruitfly — Robust ANOVA with Heterogeneous Sigma
description: Robust ANOVA with group-specific means AND sigmas; student-t family for outlier robustness.

name: Fruitfly — ANCOVA with Thorax Covariate
description: ANCOVA controlling for thorax length; `thorax_c` = centered Thorax; common slope across companion groups.

name: Fruitfly — ANHECOVA with Random Thorax Slope
description: ANHECOVA with random slope for thorax length per companion group; allows group-specific relationship between body size and longevity.

name: Salary — Two-Way Random Effects ANOVA
description: Two-way random effects ANOVA with interaction; Gaussian family; partial pooling across positions and organizations.

name: Salary — Robust ANOVA with Heterogeneous Residual Variance
formula: bf(Salary ~ 1 + (1 | Pos) + (1 | Org) + (1 | Pos:Org), sigma ~ 1 + (1 | Pos:Org))
description: Robust variant of salary ANOVA with heterogeneous residual variance per cell (Pos:Org); student-t family.

name: Split-Plot ANOVA — With Field Blocking
description: Split-plot ANOVA with tillage × fertilizer interaction plus blocking on `Field`.

name: Split-Plot ANOVA — Without Field Blocking
description: Split-plot ANOVA without explicit field blocking; comparison model to assess the contribution of the field random effect.

name: Logistic Regression — Single Predictor (Weight)
description: Logistic regression predicting sex from standardized weight; single metric predictor.

name: Logistic Regression — Two Predictors (Weight and Height)
description: Logistic regression with two metric predictors; collinear but jointly informative for predicting sex.

name: Robust Logistic Regression — Mixture with Guessing
formula: bf(male ~ a * 0.5 + (1 - a) * 1 / (1 + exp(-(b0 + b1 * weight_z))), a + b0 + b1 ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: Robust nonlinear logistic model; `a` = probability of guessing (mixture weight); identity link; estimated via `nl = TRUE`.

name: Softmax — Categorical Regression with Two Predictors
description: Categorical/softmax regression with separate intercept per category; `categorical` family.

name: Softmax — Intercepts-Only Baseline
description: Intercepts-only softmax model; estimates baseline probability per category with no predictors.

name: Conditional Logistic — Ordinal Regression (Data Set 1)
description: Sequential ordinal regression with category-specific slopes via `cs()`; `sratio` family. First conditional logistic dataset.

name: Conditional Logistic — Ordinal Regression (Data Set 2)
description: Sequential ordinal regression with category-specific slopes via `cs()`; `sratio` family. Second conditional logistic dataset.

name: Ordinal Probit — Intercept Only
description: Intercept-only ordinal probit model; thresholds estimated with `cumulative` family and no predictors.

name: Ordinal Probit — Discrimination Parameter
formula: bf(Y ~ 1 + X) + lf(disc ~ 0 + X, cmc = FALSE)
description: Ordinal model with discrimination parameter; `disc` controls category spacing and varies with X; `lf()` submodel.

name: Ordinal Probit — Heteroscedastic Gaussian Comparison
description: Heteroscedastic Gaussian comparison model; `sigma` varies with X; alternative to ordinal family.

name: Happiness and Assets — Cumulative Ordinal Probit
description: Cumulative ordinal probit with standardized assets as predictor; `Assets_s` = (Assets - mean) / sd.

name: Movie Ratings — Cumulative Ordinal Regression
description: Cumulative ordinal regression; `Year` and `Length` standardized to `Year_s` and `Length_s`.

name: Hair-Eye Color — Poisson Log-Linear
description: Poisson log-linear model with main effects and interaction as random effects; models 4×4 contingency table.

name: Hair-Eye Color — Binomial Version
description: Binomial version of the 4×4 hair-eye contingency table; `trials(264)` = total N; same random-effects structure as Poisson variant.

name: Censored Data — Missing Values Model
description: Gaussian model with missing values; brms uses listwise deletion by default. 50 MCAR missing observations out of 500.

name: Censored Data — Left/Right Censoring
description: Left/right censored Gaussian model; `cen1` ∈ {"left", "none", "right"}; censored at 85 and 115.

name: Censored Data — Interval Censoring
description: Interval censored Gaussian model; `y3` = upper bound of each interval; values rounded to nearest 5.

name: Epileptic Seizure Counts — Poisson GLMM
description: Poisson GLMM; interaction of standardised baseline × treatment; random patient intercept.

name: Epileptic Seizure Counts — Truncated Poisson
description: Same Poisson GLMM with upper truncation at 104 (the maximum possible count per visit).

name: Epileptic Seizure Counts — Simplified Main Effects
description: Simplified main-effects Poisson; omits baseline covariate; comparison model.

name: Inhaler Ordinal Ratings — Sequential Ratio Model
description: Sequential ratio ordinal model; `cs()` = category-specific coefficient for `treat`; `sratio("logit")` family estimates P(Y > k | Y ≥ k) at each threshold.

name: Kidney Recurrence Times — Lognormal Survival
formula: time | cens(censored) ~ age * sex + disease + (1 | patient)
description: Lognormal survival model; `cens()` handles right-censored observations; random intercept per patient accounts for within-patient correlation between two kidneys.

name: Heteroscedastic Model — Group-Specific Sigma
description: Gaussian with group-specific `sigma`; the sub-formula `sigma ~ 0 + x` models log(sigma) as a function of `x`.

name: Quantile Regression — Asymmetric Laplace
description: Bayesian quantile regression at the 25th percentile using an asymmetric Laplace distribution.

name: Fish Counts — Poisson Baseline
description: Poisson model for fishing trip catch counts; no zero-inflation component.

name: Fish Counts — Zero-Inflated Poisson
formula: bf(count ~ persons + child + camper, zi ~ child)
description: Zero-inflated Poisson; `zi` sub-model predicts structural-zero probability from `child`.

name: Munich Rent Data — Tensor-Product Spline
description: Tensor-product spline of area × construction year; random intercept per district.

name: Munich Rent Data — Distributional Smooth Regression
formula: bf(rentsqm ~ t2(area, yearc) + (1 | ID1 | district), sigma ~ t2(area, yearc) + (1 | ID1 | district))
description: Distributional model: both mean and log(sigma) are smooth functions; `ID1` label allows correlation between the two sets of district random effects.

name: Nonlinear Loss Development — Weibull Curve
formula: bf(cum ~ ult * (1 - exp(-(dev/theta)^omega)), ult ~ 1 + (1 | AY), omega ~ 1, theta ~ 1, nl = TRUE)
description: Weibull loss development curve; `ult` (ultimate loss) varies by accident year; `omega` = shape, `theta` = scale; `nl = TRUE` enables the nonlinear formula.

name: Multiple Membership Model — Equal Weights
description: Equal-weight multiple membership; student outcome depends equally on two schools.

name: Multiple Membership Model — Weighted
formula: y ~ 1 + (1 | mm(s1, s2, weights = cbind(w1, w2)))
description: Weighted multiple membership; `w1 + w2 = 1` for each student; weights the school random effects by the time spent at each school.

name: Rescorla-Wagner × JGET — Learning Rate vs. Delusional Ideation
description: Population-level hierarchical regression of the Rescorla-Wagner learning rate (α) on Peters Delusions Inventory (PDI) total score and session number. `(1|ID)` captures between-subject variability. α is constrained to [0,1] via logistic transformation; regression prior: Normal(0, 0.5) on PDI coefficient.  Note: `learning_rate` is a latent parameter estimated by running ActionModels on the trial-level JGET data before this regression is applied.

name: Rescorla-Wagner × JGET — Action Noise vs. Delusional Ideation
description: Population-level hierarchical regression of the Rescorla-Wagner action noise (β, response standard deviation) on PDI score and session. `(1|ID)` captures subject-level variability. β is unconstrained (exponential link); prior: Normal(0, 0.3) on intercept.

name: PVL-Delta × IGT — Learning Rate vs. Clinical Group
description: Population-level hierarchical regression of the PVL-Delta learning rate (α ∈ [0,1]) on clinical group (healthy controls, heroin, amphetamine) in the Iowa Gambling Task. `(1|subjID)` models within-subject random intercepts across trials. Transformed via logistic link; LogitNormal prior on regression coefficients.

name: PVL-Delta × IGT — Reward Sensitivity vs. Clinical Group
description: Population-level hierarchical regression of prospect-theoretic reward sensitivity (A ∈ [0,1], power parameter in utility transformation `u = |r|^A`) on clinical group in the Iowa Gambling Task. LogitNormal prior; logistic link.

name: PVL-Delta × IGT — Loss Aversion vs. Clinical Group
description: Population-level hierarchical regression of loss aversion weight (w ∈ [0,∞], scales negative prospect values as `-w·|loss|^A`) on clinical group in the Iowa Gambling Task. Exponential link; LogNormal prior on regression coefficients.

name: PVL-Delta × IGT — Action Noise vs. Clinical Group
description: Population-level hierarchical regression of the softmax inverse temperature (β ∈ [0,∞]; higher → more deterministic deck choice) on clinical group in the Iowa Gambling Task. Exponential link; LogNormal prior on regression coefficients.

name: Delay Distribution — Naive Lognormal (No Bias Correction)
description: Naive lognormal regression for delay distribution estimation (e.g. symptom onset to case notification). Does not account for interval censoring or right truncation of secondary events, producing estimates biased toward shorter delays. The `sigma` sub-model (`sigma ~ 1`) estimates the lognormal standard deviation on the log scale. Baseline model; compare with `:delay_marginal`.

name: Delay Distribution — Marginal Lognormal (Censoring + Truncation Corrected)
formula: delay_lwr | weights(n) + vreal(relative_obs_time, pwindow, swindow, delay_upr) ~ 1
description: Marginal lognormal model correcting for double interval censoring (primary and secondary event times observed only within daily windows) and right truncation (only cases with secondary event before `obs_time` are observable). Uses a custom `marginal_lognormal` brms family implemented via the `primarycensored` Stan library.  `vreal()` passes auxiliary real-valued data to the custom likelihood: observation cutoff, primary censoring window, secondary censoring window, and upper delay bound. The likelihood integrates over primary event time within the censoring window.

name: 'Epinowcast — Basic: Geometric Random Walk + Lognormal Delay'
description: Default epinowcast model for nowcasting right-truncated hospitalization counts. `enw_expectation(~0 + (1|day))` models expected final counts via a geometric random walk (daily random intercepts on the log scale). `enw_reference(~1, dist='lognormal')` fits a static lognormal delay distribution shared across all reference dates. Negative-binomial observation model with overdispersion parameter φ.

name: Epinowcast — Report Day-of-Week Effects
description: Extends the basic model with a non-parametric report date effect: `enw_report(~(1|day_of_week))` adds random intercepts for day of the week of the report date, capturing systematic under-reporting on weekends. All other components identical to `:enw_basic`.

name: Epinowcast — Non-parametric Hazard Delay Model
description: Replaces the parametric lognormal delay with a fully non-parametric discrete-time hazard model. `enw_reference(parametric=~0, non_parametric=~0+delay)` estimates a separate baseline hazard for each delay value using a Cox proportional hazards formulation. More flexible than lognormal; useful when the delay distribution is multi-modal or irregular.

name: Epinowcast — Age-Stratified Hierarchical Delays
description: Hierarchical nowcast jointly modeling three age strata. `enw_expectation(...)` includes day-of-week and daily random effects per group (`.group` notation). `enw_reference(~1 + (1|age_group))` allows lognormal delay parameters to vary by age group via partial pooling. `enw_report(...)` accounts for weekend reporting dips shared across groups.

name: Epinowcast — Time-Varying Delay with Weekly Random Walk by Age Group
description: Extends `:enw_age_reference` with time-varying delay: `rw(week, by=age_group)` adds a weekly random walk on delay parameters independently per age group, capturing temporal changes in testing and reporting practices (e.g., shifts in test positivity or lab capacity) that affect different age groups differently.

name: Epinowcast — Renewal Process with Rt Estimation
description: Mechanistic renewal-process expectation model that jointly nowcasts and estimates the instantaneous reproduction number Rₜ. `r=~1+rw(week)` specifies a weekly random walk on log(Rₜ). `generation_time=gt_pmf` provides a fixed discretised generation time PMF (Gamma-derived). `observation=~1+(1|day_of_week)` models day-of-week ascertainment variation. `enw_reference(~1, dist='lognormal')` fits a static lognormal reporting delay.

name: Baseline Nowcast — Empirical Delay Estimation
description: Non-Bayesian baseline nowcasting method using empirical delay distributions estimated from historical data. Not a regression formula — specified by two procedural arguments: `scale_factor = 3` allocates 3× max-delay time points as training data; `prop_delay = 0.5` splits training data equally between delay estimation and uncertainty quantification (retrospective error). Outputs probabilistic draws over final counts. `baselinenowcast` is designed as a reference implementation for benchmarking Bayesian nowcasters like `epinowcast`.

name: Motor Trend Cars — Gaussian Linear Model
description: `stan_glm` with default weakly-informative priors (autoscaled Normal). Demonstrates how rstanarm's prior autoscaling adapts to predictor scale. Gaussian family, identity link.

name: Cloud Seeding — Regularized Linear Model (R² Prior)
formula: rainfall ~ seeding * (sne + cloudcover + prewetness + echomotion) + time
description: `stan_lm` with an R² prior on explained variance.  Full interaction model of cloud-seeding conditions.  Gaussian family, identity link.

name: Women's Role Survey — Logistic Regression
description: `stan_glm` binomial model of survey agreement with gender-role statements as a function of education and respondent sex.  Grouped binomial with logit link.

name: Women's Role Survey — Logistic with Quadratic Education
description: Extends the linear education model with a quadratic term to capture diminishing effects at higher education levels.  Binomial / logit.

name: Child IQ — Maternal High-School Status
description: Baseline Gaussian model regressing child cognitive score on whether the mother completed high school.  Demonstrates default weakly-informative priors.

name: Child IQ — Maternal IQ
description: Regresses child test score on continuous maternal IQ; single continuous predictor. Gaussian / identity.

name: Child IQ — Maternal High-School Status and IQ
description: Additive model combining both maternal predictors.  Gaussian / identity.

name: Child IQ — Maternal High-School × IQ Interaction
description: Full interaction; the slope of maternal IQ on child score is allowed to differ by high-school completion status.  Gaussian / identity.

name: Blood Clotting Time — Gamma GLM
description: `stan_glm` with Gamma family and inverse link, modelling blood clotting time as a function of log plasma concentration, thromboplastin lot, and their interaction. Classic Dobson (2002) §9.2 example.

name: Bangladesh Wells — Logistic (Distance Only)
description: `stan_glm` logistic regression of household well-switching on distance to the nearest safe well (in units of 100 metres).  Binomial / logit.

name: Bangladesh Wells — Logistic (Distance + Arsenic)
description: Adds arsenic level of the current well as a second predictor for switching. Binomial / logit.

name: Urban Roaches — Poisson Count Model
description: `stan_glm` Poisson regression for post-treatment roach trap counts, controlling for pre-treatment baseline and senior-housing status.  Trap-exposure days enter as a log offset.  Poisson / log.

name: Urban Roaches — Negative Binomial Count Model
description: Same predictors as `:roaches_poisson` but with the negative binomial family to accommodate overdispersion and excess zeros.  `stan_glm.nb` / log.

name: Rat Weight Gain — Bayesian ANOVA (R² Prior)
description: `stan_aov` two-way factorial model with R² prior on variance explained by the protein source × protein level interaction.  Gaussian / identity.

name: Rat Weight Gain — Factors as Random Effects
description: `stan_lmer` refit treating the factorial structure as nested random intercepts, illustrating partial pooling across factor levels.  Gaussian / identity.

name: Esophageal Cancer — Ordinal Logistic Regression
description: `stan_polr` proportional-odds model of tobacco consumption group as a function of age and alcohol group.  Ordered logistic.

name: Gasoline Yield — Beta Regression (Mean Only)
description: `stan_betareg` for proportion outcome (0–1): fraction of crude oil converted to gasoline as a function of API gravity, vapor pressure, vaporization temperature, and batch factor.  Beta / logit (mean), constant precision.

name: Gasoline Yield — Distributional Beta Regression
formula: yield ~ gravity + pressure + temp10 + batch | gravity + pressure
description: Extends `:gasoline_beta` by modelling precision (`phi`) as a function of gravity and pressure.  The `|` separator follows the betareg/rstanarm distributional formula interface.  Beta / logit (mean) + log (precision).

name: Bovine Pleuropneumonia — Binomial GLMM
description: Canonical `stan_glmer` example from the rstanarm *mixed effects* vignette. Herd-level random intercept for disease incidence across 4 time periods. Binomial / logit.

name: MLB Batting 1970 — Complete Pooling
description: Complete-pooling estimate: single shared batting-average parameter for all 18 players.  Binomial / logit.  Compare with `:bball_nopooling` and `:bball_partial`.

name: MLB Batting 1970 — No Pooling
description: No-pooling model: independent intercept per player, no shrinkage. Binomial / logit.

name: MLB Batting 1970 — Partial Pooling (Hierarchical)
description: Hierarchical shrinkage model: player-level random intercepts partially pool estimates toward the population mean.  `stan_glmer` / Binomial / logit. The rstanarm *pooling* vignette shows this recovers end-of-season averages better than either complete or no pooling.

name: Pupil Dilation Experiment — Gaussian Regression
description: Gaussian regression; higher cognitive load → larger pupil dilation.

name: Spacebar-Pressing Response Times — Lognormal Regression
description: Lognormal regression; practice effect: RT decreases linearly on log scale.

name: Working Memory Recall Accuracy — Logistic Regression
description: Bernoulli(logit) regression; set-size effect on recall accuracy.

name: N400 EEG — Uncorrelated Varying Slopes
description: Varying intercepts and slopes for subjects, uncorrelated; `||` suppresses the correlation parameter between intercept and slope.

name: N400 EEG — Correlated Varying Slopes
description: Varying intercepts and correlated slopes for subjects; `|` estimates the intercept–slope correlation.

name: N400 EEG — Crossed Random Effects
description: Crossed random effects for subjects and items; both have varying intercepts and slopes.

name: N400 EEG — Distributional Model for Sigma
formula: bf(n400 ~ c_cloze + (c_cloze | subj) + (c_cloze | item), sigma ~ 1 + (1 | subj))
description: Distributional model: residual sigma modeled with a subject-level random intercept, allowing between-subject variability in residual spread.

name: Stroop Task — Lognormal Varying-Slopes Model
description: Lognormal regression; varying intercepts and correlated slopes per subject; Stroop congruence effect estimated per subject.

name: Hierarchical Pooling — Partial Pooling
description: Hierarchical / partial pooling; adaptive shrinkage across subjects.

name: Hierarchical Pooling — Complete Pooling
description: Complete pooling; single intercept ignoring subject identity.

name: Hierarchical Pooling — No Pooling
description: No pooling; one intercept per subject; cell-means parameterization.

name: Contrast Coding — Treatment Contrast
description: Factor as predictor; treatment contrast by default (reference level = "A").

name: Contrast Coding — Cell-Means Parameterization
description: Cell-means parameterization; no global intercept; each level gets its own mean.

name: Contrast Coding — Monotonic Effect
description: Monotonic effect; `F` treated as ordered categorical; `mo()` constrains the effect to be monotonically increasing or decreasing across levels.

name: 2×2 Factorial — Full Factorial Model
description: Full factorial Gaussian model: main effects of `A` and `B` plus A×B interaction.

name: 2×2 Factorial — Nested Model
description: `A` nested in `B`; `A` effects estimated separately within each level of `B`.

name: 2×2 Factorial — Logistic Regression
description: Bernoulli(logit) regression; 2×2 factorial design with binary outcome `pDV`.

name: Meta-Analysis — Random Effects Model
description: `resp_se()` passes known measurement error; `sigma = FALSE` fixes residual SD to 0; random study intercept captures between-study heterogeneity τ.

name: Individual Differences — Naive OLS
description: Naive OLS ignoring measurement error in both predictor and response; biased estimates.

name: Individual Differences — Measurement Error Model
formula: mean_rspeed | resp_se(se_rspeed, sigma = TRUE) ~ me(c_mean_pcu, se_pcu)
description: Measurement error in both response and predictor; `me()` propagates predictor uncertainty; `resp_se()` propagates response uncertainty and adds residual sigma.

name: Mixture2p — Two-Parameter Mixture Model (Set Size Effects)
formula: thetat ~ 0 + set_size + (0 + set_size | id); kappa ~ 0 + set_size + (0 + set_size | id)
description: Two-parameter mixture model for continuous report working memory data (Bays et al. 2009). The response error is decomposed into: - A von Mises (on-target memory) component with concentration `kappa` - A uniform (guessing) component with probability `1 − inv_logit(thetat)`  Both `thetat` (log-odds of remembering) and `kappa` (von Mises concentration, log scale) are regressed on set size with by-participant random slopes. The `0 + set_size` intercept-free parameterisation gives one coefficient per set-size level (treatment of set_size as factor).  bmm model spec: `mixture2p(resp_error = "error")`

name: Mixture3p — Three-Parameter Mixture Model (Non-Target Swaps)
formula: thetat ~ 0 + set_size + (0 + set_size | id); thetant ~ 0 + set_size + (0 + set_size | id); kappa ~ 0 + set_size + (0 + set_size | id)
description: Three-parameter mixture model extending `mixture2p` with a non-target swap component (Bays et al. 2009). The response error is a mixture of: - Von Mises centred on the target (memory; `thetat`, `kappa`) - Von Mises centred on a randomly selected non-target (swap; `thetant`, same `kappa`) - Uniform (guessing)  `thetant` captures log-odds of swapping to a non-target. Requires non-target feature angles (`non_target_1`–`non_target_5`) and set_size.  bmm model spec: `mixture3p(resp_error="error", nt_features=paste0("non_target_",1:5), set_size="set_size")`

name: SDM — Signal Discrimination Model (Condition Effects)
description: Signal Discrimination Model (Oberauer 2023) fit to a three-condition continuous report experiment. The SDM represents memory as a signal on a circular space; the response reflects discrimination between a memory trace and noise.  `c` (memory strength, real-valued) and `kappa` (precision, log scale) each receive one coefficient per condition via `0 + cond`. The model uses a custom circular-normal likelihood implemented via brms `stanvar()`.  bmm model spec: `sdm(resp_error = "y")`

name: IMM Full — Interference Measurement Model (All Four Parameters)
formula: c ~ 0 + cond; a ~ 0 + cond; s ~ 0 + cond; kappa ~ 0 + cond
description: Full Interference Measurement Model (Oberauer & Lin 2017) with all four parameters varying across two conditions: - `c` — baseline memory strength (item activation) - `a` — associative activation (binding strength) - `s` — spatial similarity gradient (spread of interference) - `kappa` — von Mises precision (log scale)  Each parameter gets one coefficient per condition via `0 + cond`. Non-target feature angles (`color_item2`–`color_item5`) and spatial distances (`dist_item2`–`dist_item5`) enter the likelihood directly (not as predictors in the formula).  bmm model spec: `imm(resp_error="resp_error", nt_features=paste0("color_item",2:5), set_size="set_size", nt_distances=paste0("dist_item",2:5), version="full")`

name: Single-Season Occupancy — Multi-Species with Event Covariates
formula: occ: ~ uc1 + (1 + uc1 | species); det: ~ uc1 + ec1 + (1 + uc1 + ec1 | species)
description: Single-season multi-species occupancy model with site-level (`uc1`) and visit-level (`ec1`) covariates.  - `occ` sub-model: log-odds of occupancy at a site; `uc1` as fixed slope and   random slope by species. - `det` sub-model: log-odds of detection given presence; both `uc1` and the   event-varying `ec1` with random slopes by species.  Species-level random effects pool information across the 10 species. The model returns a `brmsfit` object; all brms post-processing tools apply.  flocker call: `flock(f_occ = ~ uc1 + (1 + uc1 | species), f_det = ~ uc1 + ec1 + (1 + uc1 + ec1 | species), flocker_data = fd)`

name: Single-Season Occupancy — Multi-Species, No Event Covariates
formula: occ: ~ uc1 + (1 + uc1 | species); det: ~ uc1 + (1 + uc1 | species)
description: Single-season multi-species occupancy model with only site-level (`uc1`) covariates in both occupancy and detection sub-models (no event-varying covariate). Detection probability is constant across visits within a site, enabling an efficient "rep-constant" parameterisation in flocker.  flocker call: `flock(f_occ = ~ uc1 + (1 + uc1 | species), f_det = ~ uc1 + (1 + uc1 | species), flocker_data = fd, rep_constant = TRUE)`

name: Colonisation-Extinction — Explicit Initial Occupancy
formula: occ: ~ uc1; det: ~ uc1 + ec1; col: ~ uc1; ex: ~ uc1
description: Dynamic (multi-season) colonisation-extinction occupancy model with explicit estimation of initial occupancy. Four sub-models: - `occ` — initial occupancy at season 1 (log-odds) - `det` — detection given presence (log-odds; with event covariate) - `col` — colonisation probability (log-odds): unoccupied sites becoming occupied - `ex`  — extinction probability (log-odds): occupied sites becoming unoccupied  `multi_init = "explicit"` in flocker: initial occupancy estimated freely.  flocker call: `flock(f_occ=~uc1, f_det=~uc1+ec1, f_col=~uc1, f_ex=~uc1, flocker_data=fd, multiseason="colex", multi_init="explicit")`

name: Colonisation-Extinction — Equilibrium Initial Occupancy
formula: det: ~ uc1 + ec1; col: ~ uc1; ex: ~ uc1
description: Dynamic colonisation-extinction occupancy model where initial occupancy is derived from the colonisation/extinction equilibrium rather than estimated as a free parameter. No `occ` sub-model; initial occupancy = col / (col + ex).  `multi_init = "equilibrium"` in flocker. Reduces parameters and enforces stationarity of the occupancy process.  flocker call: `flock(f_det=~uc1+ec1, f_col=~uc1, f_ex=~uc1, flocker_data=fd, multiseason="colex", multi_init="equilibrium")`

name: Autologistic Occupancy — Equilibrium Initial Occupancy
formula: det: ~ uc1 + ec1; col: ~ uc1; auto: ~ 1
description: Autologistic dynamic occupancy model: colonisation and persistence share predictor structure; a constant logit-scale offset (`auto: ~ 1`) is added to persistence probability relative to colonisation. Initial occupancy at equilibrium.  `multiseason = "autologistic"`, `multi_init = "equilibrium"` in flocker. The autologistic formulation is more parsimonious than explicit colex when persistence and colonisation share the same predictors.  flocker call: `flock(f_det=~uc1+ec1, f_col=~uc1, f_auto=~1, flocker_data=fd, multiseason="autologistic", multi_init="equilibrium")`

name: Data-Augmented Occupancy — Species Richness Estimation
formula: occ: ~ (1 | ff_species); det: ~ uc1 + ec1 + (1 + uc1 + ec1 | ff_species)
description: Data augmentation approach for estimating total species richness from incomplete sampling. The dataset includes 50 observed species plus 50 pseudospecies (all-zero detection histories); the occupancy probability of pseudospecies reflects the probability that an unobserved species is actually present.  `ff_species` is flocker's reserved grouping keyword for species in augmented models. Occupancy random intercept by species captures species-level variation in commonness; detection random slopes by species capture variation in detectability.  flocker call: `flock(f_occ=~(1|ff_species), f_det=~uc1+ec1+(1+uc1+ec1|ff_species), flocker_data=fd, augmented=TRUE)`

name: Poisson GLM — Hierarchical Year Random Effects
description: Baseline Poisson GLM capturing inter-annual variation in rodent counts via hierarchical (random-effects) smooths on year. `s(year_fac, bs = "re") - 1` is the mgcv notation for a random intercept per year level with no overall intercept. No explicit latent trend process.  Fit with: `mvgam(count ~ s(year_fac, bs="re") - 1, family=poisson(), data=portal_train, trend_model="None")`

name: Poisson GAM — NDVI Smooth + AR(1) Latent Trend
description: State-space Poisson model separating a smooth observation-level NDVI effect from a latent AR(1) trend process. The trend captures residual temporal autocorrelation not explained by the environmental covariate.  - `obs` formula: intercept-only observation model - `trend` formula: smooth NDVI effect at the latent process level (`k = 6`   basis functions) - `trend_model = AR()`: AR(1) latent trend  Fit with: `mvgam(count ~ 1, trend_formula = ~ s(ndvi_ma12, k=6), trend_model=AR(), family=poisson(), data=portal_train)`

name: Shared Latent Trend — Multi-Series Seasonal AR(1)
formula: 'obs: count ~ series - 1 | trend: ~ s(season, bs = "cc", k = 8) [AR()]'
description: Multi-series Poisson model where all five species share a single latent AR(1) trend, with series-specific observation offsets and a cyclic seasonal spline at the trend level.  - `obs` formula: `series - 1` gives a species-specific intercept (fixed offset) - `trend` formula: cyclic cubic regression spline for seasonality (`bs = "cc"`) - `trend_model = AR()` with `trend_map` forcing all series to share one trend  The shared-trend structure is specified via a `trend_map` data.frame passed separately to `mvgam()` mapping each series to the same latent trend index.  Fit with: `mvgam(count~series-1, trend_formula=~s(season,bs="cc",k=8), trend_model=AR(), family=poisson(), data=portal_train, trend_map=trend_map)`

name: Gaussian VAR — Tensor-Product Environmental Smooths
formula: obs: y ~ -1 | trend: ~ te(temp, month, k = c(4, 4)) + te(temp, month, k = c(4, 4), by = trend) - 1 [VAR(cor = TRUE)]
description: Vector Autoregressive (VAR) model for multivariate Gaussian plankton time series with correlated process errors. Environmental forcing (temperature × month tensor product) acts at the latent process level.  - `obs` formula: no observation-level predictors - `trend` formula: shared tensor-product smooth `te(temp, month, k=c(4,4))`   plus species-specific deviations (`by = trend`); `-1` removes intercept - `trend_model = VAR(cor = TRUE)`: VAR with correlated cross-series innovations  The `by = trend` idiom in mvgam indexes each latent trend series, allowing species-specific environmental response curves.  Fit with: `mvgam(y~-1, trend_formula=~te(temp,month,k=c(4,4))+te(temp,month,k=c(4,4),by=trend)-1, trend_model=VAR(cor=TRUE), family=gaussian(), data=plankton_train)`

name: Beta AR(1) — Time-Varying Upwelling Effect on Salmon Survival
formula: obs: survival ~ 1 | trend: ~ dynamic(CUI.apr, k = 25, scale = FALSE) - 1 [AR()]
description: Beta-distributed salmon survival proportions with an AR(1) latent trend and a time-varying effect of spring upwelling index (`CUI.apr`).  - `obs` formula: intercept-only observation model (Beta family) - `trend` formula: `dynamic(CUI.apr, k=25, scale=FALSE)` makes the regression   coefficient on upwelling a smooth function of time (random-walk basis with   25 knots) - `trend_model = AR()`: AR(1) latent process in addition to the TVP  The `dynamic()` function in mvgam fits a time-varying parameter (TVP) model where the coefficient evolves as a random walk or Hilbert-space GP over time.  Fit with: `mvgam(survival~1, trend_formula=~dynamic(CUI.apr,k=25,scale=FALSE)-1, trend_model=AR(), family=betar(), data=salmon_train)`

name: N-Mixture — Smooth Detection and Abundance Sub-Models
formula: 'obs: y ~ s(det_cov, k = 4) + s(det_cov2, k = 4) | trend: ~ s(abund_cov, k = 4) + s(abund_fac, bs = "re") [nmix()]'
description: N-mixture model for imperfect detection with non-parametric smooth effects. The N-mixture likelihood jointly models the imperfect-detection observation process and the true abundance process.  - `obs` formula: detection probability sub-model; smooth effects of two   detection covariates - `trend` formula: latent abundance sub-model; smooth abundance covariate +   hierarchical random effect for the categorical habitat factor - `family = nmix()`: N-mixture likelihood (Royle 2004)  Fit with: `mvgam(y~s(det_cov,k=4)+s(det_cov2,k=4), trend_formula=~s(abund_cov,k=4)+s(abund_fac,bs="re"), family=nmix(), data=nmix_data)`

name: Sleep Deprivation — Correlated Random Slopes
description: LMM with correlated by-subject random slope and intercept for `Days`. `(Days | Subject)` fits one 2×2 random-effects covariance matrix per subject.  ```r lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy) ```

name: Sleep Deprivation — Uncorrelated Random Slopes
description: LMM with **uncorrelated** by-subject random slope and intercept. `(Days || Subject)` constrains the off-diagonal covariance to zero (diagonal random-effects covariance matrix).  ```r lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject), data = sleepstudy) ```

name: Dyestuff — Minimal Random-Intercept LMM
description: The simplest possible LMM: grand-mean intercept plus a random intercept for each batch. Introductory example in Bates et al. (JSS 2015, §2).  ```r lmer(Yield ~ 1 + (1 | Batch), data = Dyestuff) ```

name: CBPP — Binomial GLMM (lme4 syntax)
description: Binomial GLMM for CBPP incidence using lme4's matrix-response `cbind` syntax. Contrast with the brms equivalent: `incidence | trials(size) ~ period + (1|herd)`.  ```r glmer(cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ period + (1 | herd),       family = binomial, data = cbpp) ```

name: Penicillin — Crossed Random Intercepts
description: LMM with two fully **crossed** random intercepts (plates and samples). Neither grouping factor is nested within the other.  ```r lmer(diameter ~ 1 + (1 | plate) + (1 | sample), data = Penicillin) ```

name: Pastes — Nested Random Effects
description: LMM with nested random effects. `batch/cask` expands to `(1|batch) + (1|batch:cask)`; casks are identified locally within each batch, not globally.  ```r lmer(strength ~ (1 | batch/cask), data = Pastes) ```

name: Verbal Aggression — Bernoulli GLMM, Crossed Random Effects
formula: r2 ~ Anger + Gender + btype + situ + (1 | id) + (1 | item)
description: Bernoulli GLMM with two fully crossed random intercepts (subjects × items). `r2` is recoded to integer 0/1 from Y/N.  ```r glmer(r2 ~ Anger + Gender + btype + situ + (1|id) + (1|item),       family = binomial, data = VerbAgg) ```

name: Contraception — Binomial GLMM with Random Slopes
formula: use ~ age + I(age^2) + livch + urban + (urban | district)
description: Binomial GLMM for contraception use with a random slope for `urban` within district — allowing the urban/rural gap to vary across districts. `use` is recoded from Y/N to integer 0/1.  ```r glmer(use ~ age + I(age^2) + livch + urban + (urban | district),       family = binomial, data = Contraception) ```

name: Dyestuff — Minimal Random-Intercept LMM
description: The canonical introductory LMM in MixedModels.jl: one variance component for batch-to-batch variability, no fixed covariates.  ```julia fit(LinearMixedModel, @formula(Yield ~ 1 + (1 | Batch)), dyestuff) ```  Note: MixedModels.jl's bundled copy uses lowercase `yield`/`batch`; the Rdatasets CSV uses `Yield`/`Batch`.

name: Sleep Deprivation — Correlated Random Slopes
description: LMM with correlated by-subject random slope and intercept for `Days`. Idiomatic MixedModels.jl style writes explicit `1 +` intercepts.  ```julia fit(LinearMixedModel, @formula(Reaction ~ 1 + Days + (1 + Days | Subject)), sleepstudy) ```

name: Sleep Deprivation — Uncorrelated Random Slopes (zerocorr)
description: Same as the correlated model but with the off-diagonal covariance forced to zero. MixedModels.jl uses `zerocorr()` instead of lme4's `(x || g)` syntax.  ```julia fit(LinearMixedModel,     @formula(Reaction ~ 1 + Days + zerocorr(1 + Days | Subject)), sleepstudy) ```

name: Penicillin — Crossed Random Intercepts
description: LMM with two fully crossed random intercepts. Neither `plate` nor `sample` is nested within the other; both random intercepts appear additively.  ```julia fit(LinearMixedModel,     @formula(diameter ~ 1 + (1 | plate) + (1 | sample)), penicillin) ```

name: Pastes — Nested Random Effects
description: LMM with nested random effects: `batch/cask` expands to `(1|batch) + (1|batch:cask)`. Cask labels are local to each batch.  ```julia fit(LinearMixedModel, @formula(strength ~ 1 + (1 | batch/cask)), pastes) ```

name: Verbal Aggression — Bernoulli GLMM, Crossed Random Effects
formula: r2 ~ 1 + Anger + Gender + btype + situ + (1 | id) + (1 | item)
description: Bernoulli GLMM with two crossed random intercepts (subjects × items). `r2` recoded from Y/N to integer 0/1.  ```julia fit(GeneralizedLinearMixedModel,     @formula(r2 ~ 1 + Anger + Gender + btype + situ + (1|id) + (1|item)),     verbagg, Bernoulli()) ```

name: Contraception — Bernoulli GLMM with Polynomial Age
formula: use ~ 1 + age + abs2(age) + livch + urban + (1 | district)
description: Bernoulli GLMM for contraception use in Bangladesh. MixedModels.jl uses `abs2()` (squaring function) inside `@formula` instead of R's `I(age^2)`. `use` recoded from Y/N to integer 0/1.  ```julia fit(GeneralizedLinearMixedModel,     @formula(use ~ 1 + age + abs2(age) + livch + urban + (1|district)),     contraception, Bernoulli()) ```

name: Cement — Gaussian Linear Model (no random effects)
description: `inla()` with `family = "gaussian"` — the simplest INLA use case, equivalent to `lm()` but with Bayesian inference via INLA. Demonstrates default weakly-informative priors on regression coefficients.

name: Penicillin — Gaussian GLMM with IID Random Intercept
description: `f(plate_id, model = "iid")` specifies exchangeable random intercepts per assay plate — the INLA equivalent of `(1|plate)` in lme4.  Gaussian family.

name: Sleep Deprivation — Gaussian GLMM with IID Random Intercept
description: Random intercept per subject; `subject_id` is the numeric version of `Subject`. Gaussian family.  Equivalent to `lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1|Subject))`.

name: Sleep Deprivation — Gaussian GLMM with IID Random Slopes
description: Random slopes model: `f(subject_id, Days, ...)` specifies subject-specific slopes for `Days` — the INLA way of writing `(0 + Days | Subject)`.  Gaussian family.

name: Airline Passengers — Random Walk (RW1) Temporal Smoothing
description: First-order random walk latent field on the time index `t`; the intercept is absorbed into the random walk (hence `0 +`).  Gaussian family.  Equivalent to a Bayesian smoothing spline.

name: Airline Passengers — Random Walk (RW2) Temporal Smoothing
description: Second-order random walk; smoother than RW1, penalises second differences. Equivalent to cubic spline smoothing.  Gaussian family.

name: Airline Passengers — AR(1) Temporal Process
description: Latent AR(1) process over time.  Estimates autocorrelation parameter ρ jointly with the observation variance.  Gaussian family.

name: Airline Passengers — Seasonal Latent Field
description: Seasonal latent field with period 12 months (sum-to-zero constraint within each year).  Captures multiplicative seasonality on the log scale.  Gaussian family.

name: VA Lung Cancer — Weibull Survival Model
formula: inla.surv(time, status) ~ trt + celltype + karno + diagtime + age + prior
description: `inla.surv()` wraps right-censored event times for INLA's survival families. Weibull proportional hazards model (`family = "weibullsurv"`); the shape parameter is estimated as a hyperparameter.

name: LIDAR — Nonparametric Regression via RW2
description: 1D nonparametric regression using a second-order random walk latent field over the continuous predictor `range`.  `constr = FALSE` drops the sum-to-zero constraint; `-1` removes the fixed intercept (absorbed by the random walk). Gaussian family.  Compare with spline-based approaches.

name: Hospital Mortality — Binomial IID Overdispersion
description: 12-hospital mortality benchmark.  `f(hospital, model = "iid")` with `family = "binomial"` (trials = `n`) shrinks small-hospital rates toward the population mean.  Demonstrates PC priors on the precision hyperparameter.

name: Boston Housing — Gaussian Spatial (ICAR / Besag)
formula: log(medv) ~ crim + zn + indus + chas + nox + rm + age + dis + rad + tax + ptratio + black + lstat + f(id, model = 'besag', graph = W)
description: Intrinsic CAR (Besag) spatial random effect for 506 Boston census tracts. `f(id, model = "besag", graph = W)` requires an adjacency matrix `W` (spdep object) passed separately — it is not contained in the tabular data. Gaussian family.  Also fitted with `"bym"` (BYM = ICAR + IID) for comparison.

name: Phenoloxidase — Gaussian GLMM with Full-Sib Family Random Effect
description: Intercept-only fixed effects; `~FSfamily` random intercept partitions phenoloxidase variance into between-family and within-family components.  Gaussian family. Textbook introductory example from the MCMCglmm reference manual.

name: Blue Tit Tarsus — Gaussian GLMM with Foster-Nest Random Intercept
